questions.question: What happens to a class instance sent to a worker with postMessage?
options: It arrives with its prototype and methods intact
It is shared by reference between both threads
postMessage throws because objects cannot be sent
It is structured-cloned and arrives as a plain object without its prototype or methods
questions.explanation: postMessage uses the structured clone algorithm, which copies data properties but drops prototypes. Functions cannot be cloned at all (DataCloneError).

questions.question: After `worker.postMessage(buffer, [buffer])`, what is `buffer.byteLength` in the sending thread?
options: 0, because the buffer was transferred and is now detached
Unchanged, because a copy was sent
undefined, because the variable is deleted
questions.explanation: Listing the buffer in the transfer list moves ownership to the worker instead of copying it, leaving the sender with a detached, zero-length buffer.

questions.question: What must a page do before browsers expose SharedArrayBuffer to it?
options: Be cross-origin isolated by sending COOP: same-origin and COEP: require-corp headers
Run only inside a service worker
questions.explanation: Because shared memory enables high-resolution timing attacks like Spectre, browsers require cross-origin isolation, which you can check with self.crossOriginIsolated.

questions.question: Which statement about Atomics is correct?
options: Atomics.wait is the recommended way to pause the browser main thread
Atomics only work on regular ArrayBuffers
Atomics.wait throws on the browser main thread; Atomics.waitAsync is the non-blocking alternative
questions.explanation: Blocking the UI thread is disallowed, so Atomics.wait throws there. Atomics operations such as add, load, wait and notify operate on typed arrays over shared memory.
